newsitem.title: JAPAN: DuPont, Mitsui polyethylene plant shut after fire.
newsitem.headline: DuPont, Mitsui polyethylene plant shut after fire.

text.p: A polyethylene plant owned jointly by DuPont Co and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd in Hiroshima Prefecture, western Japan, was shut down after a fire broke out early Friday, a spokesman for the joint venture said.

Vapourised ethylene was released from safety valves after pressure built up inside a reactor that converts ethylene to polyethylene, and the unit caught fire at 2.00 a.m. (1700 GMT) on Friday, he said.
The fire was brought under control after about 15 minutes.
No one was injured, and no facilities were damaged by the fire.
It was unclear when the plant, with an annual production capacity of 70,000 tonnes, could resume operations, as an investigation by local authorities is underway, he said.
Mitsui Petrochemical's Chiba plant, near Tokyo, supplies the Hiroshima plant with feedstock ethylene, he added.
The Chiba plant has an ethylene output capacity of 553,000 tonnes per year.
